findings.reason: it moves the generic half into machine_artifact.py and makes §7's done-when name which parts are per-machine (IDS assembly) versus generic, which is the reusability claim §7 exists to establish.
findings.text: machine-agnostic machinery (_ghcr_repository_parts, _write_publication_recipe, _write_and_verify_ids, _artifact_digests) sits in the DIII-D-specific front-end while the shared owner nova/imas/machine_artifact.py holds only the lifecycle; §7's own ruling ("machine-parameterised and serves both machines through one path, rather than a second machine-specific copy beside it") is not satisfied for the publication and digest path, so a third machine copies 500 lines

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §5 kernel library is one module (nova/equilibrium/map_extraction.py) hiding the operator, per-surface separation, masking, chord sampling and their receipts behind four public functions; the layers consume each other rather than repeating.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §7 design commits to "one path, not a second machine-specific copy", but publication-recipe and digest machinery that is not machine-specific lives in the 513-line DIII-D-only script beside a 383x smaller MAST one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched before proposing: decision pins cite prior art, followup f-dfo-seam-survey ran a 20-capability cross-repo survey against pinned ambix 2f3dcd0c, and comment c-20260817 recorded a live duplicate audit; the code confirms the consolidations landed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every apparent wrapper carries added behaviour: apply_delta_star adds the uniform-axis validation, interior mask and the -Δ*/(2π μ0 R) current-density conversion, and observation_kernels reuses map_extraction.sample_chord_psi_norm instead of re-deriving chord sampling.
